_comment: Aelgard Glass Desert bestiary. Crystalline wasteland where the sand is fused into prism-shards and dragons refract light. Tone: blinding, silent, hostile to iron. Threats here test eyes and resistance to magic.
_region_tone: blinding-white glare, silent crystal-crack underfoot, everything made of fused silica. Reflections are not always honest.

monsters.name: Prism elemental
monsters.examine: A being of pure refracted light.
bible: Prism elementals form in sunstruck pockets of the Glass Desert where three or more crystalline surfaces intersect at the right angles. They are localised weather as much as life: dispel the sun or break the angles and the elemental vanishes.
They attack by refracted light — directing amplified sun against a target. The attack is blocked by any reflective polish.
Killing one releases the stored light in a brief, non-damaging flash that is readable from miles away. Glass Desert guides use prism-kills as signal flares.
monsters.habitat: sun-trap crystal pockets, specifically the Refracted Flats and the Wall of Nine Angles
monsters.reagent_callout: Refracted essence (1/10) — reagent for the mirror-cloak (light-damage immunity, Glass Desert-niche).

monsters.name: Crystal dragon
monsters.examine: A dragon with crystalline scales. Refracts magic.
bible: Crystal dragons evolved from sand wyverns over thirty generations of Glass Desert adaptation. Their scales are grown silica, effectively prism-armor. Magic cast at a crystal dragon refracts off the scale and strikes a bystander.
Solo-hunting a crystal dragon is safer than group-hunting one; the refract mechanic punishes flank positioning.
Their breath is not fire but a sweeping beam of amplified light, which sets flammable materials alight at range.
monsters.habitat: the Shard Spires, the Great Glass Flats, the deep interior beyond the sun-walkable zone
monsters.reagent_callout: Crystal dragon scale (1/32 collection-log) — reagent for the Glass Desert ultimate shield 'The Ninth Angle' (magic-reflect back at attacker).

monsters.name: Sand wraith
monsters.examine: An ancient spirit of the Glass Desert.
bible: Sand wraiths are the ghosts of ancient Glass Desert travellers — not corpses, but compressed memories of journeys taken. Each wraith represents a single crossing that ended badly.

A wraith can be appeased by telling it, truthfully, that the crossing in question has been completed by someone else. This requires the player to look up the relevant crossing-log, which is archived at the Glass Desert Ranger Station.
Appeased wraiths yield their grudge-fragment willingly and vanish. Combat kills yield a different, corrupted fragment.
monsters.habitat: crossing-routes, old caravan-tracks, the Seventh Ridge
monsters.reagent_callout: Sand-wraith grudge (1/16, appeasement yields pure, combat yields corrupted — different downstream recipes).

monsters.name: Sunking
monsters.examine: The ghost of a king who claimed the sun.
bible: The Sunking is a single named boss: the ghost of a pre-Crown monarch who, in his final decree, claimed the sun as the property of his line. The claim was never honored, but the ghost has not surrendered it.
He fights only at noon. At other times he is invisible, immobile, and reciting the decree to himself. Only the noon hour permits him to project his claim outward as combat.
Killing the Sunking is a one-time event. Once defeated, he is gone. His decree remains legally contested in Crown archives.
monsters.habitat: the Sunking's Pavilion, the exact centre of the Glass Desert, only at noon (game-clock)
monsters.reagent_callout: Sunking's crown (1/1 one-shot drop) — reagent for a single unique 'Sun-claimed' crown (light-damage buff, once only; account-bound).

monsters.name: Mirage knight
monsters.examine: A knight of a kingdom that never existed.
bible: Mirage knights are the Glass Desert's most elaborate optical illusion — fully-formed armoured warriors that exist only at specific sun-angle/wind-speed combinations. They fight with full material presence when the conditions are right.
A knight can be dispelled by introducing dust into the air (disrupting the light). Glass Desert tacticians carry dust-bombs for exactly this purpose.
Engaged in melee by a player without dust, the knight will fight to death and leave behind a small quantity of desert-glass as residue.
monsters.habitat: sun-angle zones, the Mirage Fields, the afternoon approaches to the Shard Spires
monsters.anti_pattern_note: dust-bomb counter is a core counterplay. Encounter should not spawn knights in environments where dust is trivially available.

monsters.name: Shard crawler
monsters.examine: A crab of shards. Small, sharp, plentiful.
bible: Shard crawlers are crab-like animals that nest inside fused silica rubble. They are the Glass Desert's most common encounter and the first threat a new crossing-rookie meets.
A single shard crawler is trivial. A swarm is not, and shard crawlers swarm reliably when one is killed — the sound of broken carapace attracts every crawler within 60 paces.
Veteran crossers kill shard crawlers by crushing, not cutting, because cutting makes more noise.
monsters.habitat: silica rubble-fields, any broken-shard terrain, caravan-rest areas
monsters.anti_pattern_note: sound-swarm mechanic. Slash weapons attract waves; crush weapons do not.

monsters.name: Mirror fiend
monsters.examine: A demon-kin who entered a mirror and never left.
bible: Mirror fiends are not Glass Desert natives. They are demons from elsewhere who crossed through a mirror-surface and, per the rules of whatever they entered, cannot leave through the same surface.

They live inside reflective surfaces in the Glass Desert, appearing when a reflective object is held at the correct angle. Fighting one requires engaging from within the mirror's spatial projection — effectively, fighting on the other side of a looking-glass.
Smashing the reflective object that hosts the fiend kills it. Smashing a mirror-fiend directly does nothing.
monsters.habitat: polished surfaces, specifically the Mirror Market and the Scryer's Maze
monsters.reagent_callout: Mirror-fiend glass (1/18, only obtained via mirror-break not combat) — reagent for the Mirror-Fiend Dagger (ignores magic reflection on crystal-tag enemies).

monsters.name: Dune scarab queen
monsters.examine: The matriarch of a shard-nest. Large, gold-rimmed, coordinated.
bible: Each shard-crawler nest is ruled by a dune scarab queen — a larger, gold-rimmed specimen that coordinates the swarm. Queens do not leave their nests in ordinary circumstances.
A queen defends by deploying swarms of shard crawlers in waves. Killing waves consumes player resources until the queen emerges for a final confrontation.
Queen-shell is a prized Glass Desert material. Cut and polished, it refracts light in deliberate patterns, which is the basis for the Glass Desert's signalling lanterns.
monsters.habitat: shard-crawler mega-nests, specifically the Broken Crescent and the Shardheart warren
monsters.reagent_callout: Scarab queen shell (1/48 collection-log) — reagent for the Scarab-lantern (long-range signal device, used in several Glass Desert quests).

monsters.name: Sunstalker
monsters.examine: A hawk that hunts by sun-heat, not sight.
bible: Sunstalkers are raptor-kin that hunt by detecting heat differentials. They strike any warm body crossing the Glass Desert in noontime — which is everything.
Their plumage is nearly black, absorbing sun-heat efficiently. A sunstalker descending from above is a visible dark speck at distance.
Their feathers, stripped, make exceptional fletching for arrows — sunstalker-fletched arrows fly noticeably faster than standard.
monsters.habitat: high thermals above the desert, specifically 300+ paces above ground
monsters.reagent_callout: Sunstalker feather (1/5) — reagent for fast-fletch arrow variant.

monsters.name: Glasshand golem
monsters.examine: A golem of hand-sized shards. Reassembles.
bible: Glasshand golems are distributed creatures — their body is a collection of hand-sized shard-hands connected by a binding-thought rather than physical linkage. Damage separates hands; a separated hand drifts, relocates, and re-joins.
Killing a glasshand requires shattering enough hands faster than they can re-join. The math is: destroy 80% of the hands within 30 seconds.
Fragments of glasshand retain their animating thought weakly; a salvaged glasshand finger will, if held, point toward the nearest golem in any direction.
monsters.habitat: the Hand-Fields, distributed across the southern Glass Desert
monsters.anti_pattern_note: area-of-effect crush weapons are strongly preferred. Single-target attacks fail against reassembly.

monsters.name: Crystal serpent
monsters.examine: A snake of crystal. Cold. Sharp. Patient.
bible: Crystal serpents are the apex ground-predator of the outer Glass Desert. Snake-shaped, crystal-bodied, venomless but lethally sharp-fanged. They hunt by patience — they can hold still for 12 hours waiting for a target to come within strike-range.
They are cold; surface temperature roughly equal to air temperature. This makes them difficult to detect by heat-sight (the sunstalker strategy).
Their skin, shed seasonally, is a durable crystalline leather. Veteran rangers collect shed skin in preference to combat — the shed is free and the serpent is still alive.
monsters.habitat: sun-warmed rocks, predator-heaped dunes, the ambush zones along the Whistle Path
monsters.reagent_callout: Crystal serpent shed (1/10) — reagent for crystal-scale boots (magic-defence footwear).

monsters.name: Nomad glassmaker
monsters.examine: A nomad craftsman. Would rather trade than fight.
bible: Nomad glassmakers are itinerant Glass Desert crafters — small-cart, two-camel operations that travel between crystal deposits and buy shards from hunters. They are passive and often extraordinarily useful to travellers.

A glassmaker will trade raw crystals for worked items, small commissions for favours, and (rarely) travel-routes for gossip. Killing one is both stupid and taboo; the other nomads will remember the face.
They know every route through the desert. A glassmaker-friend is one of the most valuable allies a Glass Desert adventurer can cultivate.
monsters.habitat: nomad-cart routes, specifically the three main traderails between shard-fields
monsters.anti_pattern_note: passive, valuable NPC-like interactions. NEVER auto-aggro. Slayer tasks on glassmakers should trigger abort flow.

Sunking's crown (1/1 one-shot — account-bound Sun-claimed crown)
Scarab queen shell (1/48 collection-log — reagent: Scarab-lantern)
